periods.public: The committee discusses the need for a data-driven approach to the new fee structure. They agree to divide the research to cover financial stability, administrative burden, and member attendance patterns.

lines.Mio: Suggests they look at the numbers first to avoid guessing.
lines.Jonathan: Agrees and suggests looking at attendance trends.
lines.Takumi: Wants to know who is actually doing the work.
lines.Toshio: Suggests checking the administrative load on the treasurer.
lines.Kenji: Wants to see why some people don't join.

lines.Mio: Chooses Last year's ledger of outgoings and Bank statements on last year's renewals.
lines.Jonathan: Chooses Weekday turnout since the summer outings and Quieter members at the winter social.
lines.Takumi: Chooses Tally of the sign-in sheets and The rota against the attendance record.
lines.Toshio: Chooses Outgoing treasurer's logged hours and Sign-up records for mid-year joiners.
lines.Kenji: Chooses Taster evening forms from non-joiners and Minute books from the named-grade years.

periods.public: Participants share their findings. They debate the tension between reducing the treasurer's workload, maintaining accessibility for newcomers, and addressing the unfairness of high-usage members paying the same as inactive ones.

lines.Mio: Reveals that most costs are fixed and some members struggle with lump sums.
lines.Jonathan: Notes that charging per event discouraged weekday attendance.
lines.Takumi: Points out that a small group does all the attending and the work.
lines.Toshio: Highlights the massive time sink of chasing small payments.
lines.Kenji: Mentions that tiered systems caused friction and high entry costs deter newcomers.

lines.Mio: Asks @Toshio if a simple system would save time.
lines.Jonathan: Warns @Takumi that punishing low attendance might alienate people.
lines.Takumi: Argues that the current system is unfair to the regulars.
lines.Toshio: Confirms that chasing individual fees is the biggest burden.
lines.Kenji: Expresses concern about making membership feel like a hierarchy.

lines.Mio: Suggests they need a balance between simplicity and fairness.
lines.Jonathan: Questions if a flat fee is too high for some.
lines.Takumi: Asks if there is a way to reward the regulars.
lines.Toshio: Argues for the most administratively efficient method.
lines.Kenji: Wants to ensure the club remains welcoming to all.

periods.public: The committee evaluates the three proposed options against the discovered data. They weigh the administrative ease of a single payment against the flexibility of per-event costs and the perceived fairness of tiers.

lines.Mio: Argues that a single fee covers fixed costs reliably.
lines.Jonathan: Supports a system that doesn't make people hesitate to attend.
lines.Takumi: Prefers a system that distinguishes levels of use.
lines.Toshio: Strongly advocates for the option with the least paperwork.
lines.Kenji: Suggests a low base fee to keep it open to newcomers.

lines.Mio: Points out that tiered systems might be too complex to manage.
lines.Jonathan: Agrees with Mio, citing the risk of alienating quiet members.
lines.Takumi: Questions why the regulars should subsidize the inactive.
lines.Toshio: Reminds Takumi that managing tiers or events is a treasurer's nightmare.
lines.Kenji: Worries that a high flat fee will scare off taster-evening guests.

lines.Mio: Suggests a flat fee is the safest bet for the budget.
lines.Jonathan: Agrees that simplicity fosters a better atmosphere.
lines.Takumi: Reluctantly admits that administrative collapse helps no one.
lines.Toshio: Urges a vote for the most efficient option.
lines.Kenji: Still hopes for a more flexible approach but sees the logic.

seats.Mio: Wants financial predictability and stability. She pushes for a system that ensures fixed costs are covered without guesswork.
seats.Toshio: Focused on minimizing the administrative burden. He argues against any system that requires constant chasing of small sums.
seats.Jonathan: Cares about the psychological barrier to attendance. He opposes any structure that makes members weigh the cost of coming out.
seats.Takumi: Concerned with fairness and the imbalance of contribution. He initially seeks a way to differentiate between heavy and light users.
seats.Kenji: Values inclusivity and low barriers to entry. He worries about social hierarchies and the deterrent effect of high upfront costs.
